title: ci: add signed artifact pipeline, SBOMs and provenance for private installer releases
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Private deployments require cryptographically verifiable release artifacts (installer tarballs, Helm charts, OCI images) plus reproducible provenance and SBOMs for audit/compliance. This PR implements an end-to-end pipeline that builds installer artifacts, generates SBOMs, produces in-toto provenance attestations, and signs artifacts with sigstore/cosign. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private need supply-chain guarantees (artifact origin, immutable signatures, SBOM for vulnerability/audit teams) and an automated release manifest that operators can consume to install/upgrade/rollback reliably. What this PR does: - Adds a GitHub Actions workflow ( .github/workflows/release-private-installer.yml ) that performs build -> test -> sbom -> provenance -> sign -> publish steps for private-installer releases. - Uses syft to generate SBOMs (spdx/json) for installer tarballs and container artifacts. - Emits in-toto provenance attestation (metalink style) capturing build inputs and exact source commit. - Signs both artifacts and provenance with cosign (Sigstore) using repository-bound ephemeral keys where available, and falls back to a KMS-backed key for release branches. - Produces a single signed release manifest (JSON) that lists artifacts, checksums, SBOM links, provenance attestations, and cosign signatures. - Publishes Helm chart OCI artifacts to internal registry (chartmuseum/internal-oci) and stores tarballs in the private S3 bucket with lifecycle and retention. - Adds helper scripts (scripts/sign-artifacts.sh, scripts/verify-release.sh) for on-prem operators to verify signatures and SBOMs during install/upgrade. - Adds CI validators that verify manifest signatures and SBOM presence before marking a release green. Migration notes / compatibility: - Backwards compatible: existing installer tarballs can still be built locally; operators who don't consume signed manifests are unaffected. - Release process is opt-in via the release workflow dispatch and protected by repo permissions. Testing: - Integration job runs installer acceptance tests against a local kind cluster and a minimal VPC config in the test account. - End-to-end verification validates that the signed release manifest can be used to fetch artifacts, verify cosign signatures, and validate SBOMs. Checklist (implemented in PR): - [x] Build artifact step and deterministic build flags - [x] SBOM generation (syft) - [x] In-toto provenance generation - [x] Cosign signing step with verification - [x] Publish release manifest to releases.redwood.internal - [x] Helm/OCI chart push to internal registry - [x] Add scripts/docs for operators - [x] CI validators to fail on missing SBOM/signature Known constraints and followups: - The KMS key rotation flow is documented in docs/private-deploy/supplychain-keys.md but will be automated in a follow-up (ENG-1902). - We currently rely on GitHub Actions runners with access to an ephemeral sigstore token; we plan to add a Jenkins fallback for air-gapped customers. Links: Linear ENG-1873, Security design doc: docs/security/supply-chain.md, Release manifest schema: docs/private-deploy/release-manifest-schema.md
